statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail risk of 9% stays well below the block threshold: Globex reopened at 22:00Z without a gap and NQ has held a 47-point band since, while cross-asset stress remains extreme on Brent at $101.96 and a 10-year Treasury yield at a three-year high of 4.837%.
recommendation: Conditions are described as two-way and range-bound at the assessment cutoff. The US cash session is closed, the CME maintenance halt has ended, the Globex reopen produced no gap despite the live US-Iran exchange in the Gulf, and every scheduled index-level catalyst of September 9 has cleared. The narrow evidence-based danger window falls on the September 10 producer price and jobless claims release at 12:30Z and the US cash open that follows it.
headline: Nasdaq-100 futures reopen without a gap after a third shallow down day, with stress carried by $102 Brent and a three-year-high 10-year yield rather than by index structure
body:
Globex has reopened. NQ front-month futures trade 29,428.25, -0.07%, inside a 29,425.75-29,472.75 range off a 29,458.50 reopen, a band roughly 47 points wide in the first half hour of the new session. There is no reopen gap and no directional efficiency, and that matters more than the direction: the failure mode the tail score measures requires shallow pullbacks and repeated extension after failed retracements, and the reopen has produced neither. It follows a US cash session that did the same thing. NDX closed 29,421.55, -0.29% against the 29,507.70 previous close, within ten points of its 29,431.94 open after a 29,334.40-29,563.60 range, so both session extremes were retraced rather than extended. This was a third consecutive down day for the majors, with the Dow -0.77% at 52,380.66 and the S&P 500 -0.48% at 7,636.36 both weaker than the Nasdaq-100, but the decline stayed shallow at index level. VIX closed 16.46, +4.71%, a low absolute level for an extreme-stress reading.

Stress is carried almost entirely by cross-asset conditions. Brent trades $101.96 and WTI $97.06, +3.25%, after the US destroyed five Iranian oil tankers and struck targets near the Kharg Island export hub, with reported Strait of Hormuz throughput down from about nine million barrels a day in late August to under two million. The 10-year Treasury yield sits at 4.837% after touching 4.857%, a three-year high, and the 30-year is around 5.3%, with the long end pressured further after the Treasury announced an enlarged but still small $6bn buyback of longer-dated debt. Megacap behaviour was dispersed rather than aligned, with Meta up more than six percent on its Muse consumer AI agent launch against Alphabet -2.3% and Amazon -1.8%, and semiconductor performance was split. Dispersion of that kind lowers directional conviction and raises stress; it does not by itself produce the persistent one-way path that would overwhelm mean reversion.

The geopolitical situation is a genuine discontinuity risk and is the reason tail is not lower. An active military exchange in the Gulf remains the standing channel for an overnight gap through the thinnest liquidity of the horizon. Against that, the observed evidence is a market that has repeatedly retraced its extremes. The horizon peak falls on September 10, where the mapped policy state moves to WATCH across the 12:30Z producer price and jobless claims release and the 13:30Z US cash open, with a secondary lift into the 17:00Z 30-year bond auction and the 17:40Z buyback operation. No future price path, release outcome or headline is asserted as already observed.

lookbackSummary: The prior 24 hours were quiet through the US evening and the Asian session, with tail between 6% and 9% and stress climbing from 71% to 79% as crude cleared $100 and Treasury yields extended. Tail peaked at 20% in the 12:00Z hour on a trend-down European tape, then eased once the US cash session produced genuine two-way price discovery, holding between 10% and 17% through the afternoon and finishing at 9% for the closing hour. Stress stayed between 80% and 83% for the last twelve published hours. The 10:00Z hour has no published Claude assessment and is marked unavailable.
outlookSummary: The current hour covers the Globex reopen, which has so far produced no gap and a 47-point range, so conditional tail stays at its post-close low. Risk then decays toward the single-digit overnight baseline the preceding cycle actually produced, with thin Asian liquidity left as a headline-gap channel rather than a trend channel. It rebuilds stepwise through the European morning into the horizon peak on September 10, where the WATCH state is mapped across the 12:30Z producer price and jobless claims release and the 13:30Z US cash open. Conditional tail then decays through the US morning before a secondary lift into the 17:00Z 30-year bond auction and the 17:40Z Treasury buyback operation, easing again into the close. No future price path, release outcome or headline is asserted as already observed.

That absence of directional efficiency, after a cash session that retraced both extremes, holds tail at its post-close low.

forecast.analysis: European morning. Conditional tail held. The prior cycle's European weakness was absorbed once US price discovery began, which is the specific reason this hour is scored as elevated-but-contained rather than at a blocking level. Applying that pattern forward is an assumption, not an observation.
drivers: Prior-cycle pattern: European weakness absorbed by US two-way discovery
Pattern application is an assumption, not observed structure for this hour

Conditional tail holds at the watch level because that stacking is exactly where a delayed second leg would form, if one forms at all.
